_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THIS GATE IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the repository
root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
tools/one-machine/injection-sweep.json
WHAT IS BROKEN BELOW IS EVERY DEFENCE WHOSE FAILURE IS SILENT, and here that
is nearly all of them. This gate's whole subject is a state that reports zero
findings: no machine was asked, the machine that answered was this one, the
answer is about bytes that have since changed, the run has not ended. Each of
those, if the check goes, turns into a clean pass — so a case that passes
because its fixture is convenient rather than because the code is right would
leave the lane looking exactly as it does when it works.
TWO OF THE PAIRS BELOW ARE DELIBERATELY OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS OF ONE FACT. The
fingerprint must move with the working tree and must NOT move with `HEAD`,
and a sweep that only broke one of those would be half a sweep: the first
makes a stale answer read as current, and the second makes every answer read
as stale, which is a gate that refuses forever and looks like one working.
ONE DEFENCE BELOW IS A SHAPE AND NOT A LINE, so it has no injection and
says so here rather than being quietly absent. `run_bounded` gives its
child FILES rather than pipes, and a pipe held open by a run the child
detached is what would make the budget meaningless — but there is no line
to break, because the pipes are not there at all. That is the point of the
shape; the case that would fail is still written
(`output_held_open_by_something_the_child_left_behind…`).
Scoped to this crate's own suite: nothing here touches the tree it judges.
THE RED SETS ARE EXHAUSTIVE AND THEY ARE MEASURED RATHER THAN INTENDED —
running this manifest narrower names the missing reds and running it wider
names the new ones, and a subset claim is silent in both directions.

injections.name: a-census-taken-here-answers-for-a-second-machine
injections.why: the premise of the whole crate in one line. Every defect this repository has found in the census was found somewhere its author was not sitting, and an answer from the machine that wrote the gate is the answer the gate already had — a second opinion that is the first one again, printed as though it were evidence

edits.to: if header.host.eq_ignore_ascii_case("a name no machine has") {

injections.name: a-census-about-other-bytes-answers-for-these
injections.why: the staleness direction. A verdict about a tree that has since changed is not a verdict about this one, and it is the state a lane like this spends most of its time in — the dispatch is per commit and the tree moves between rounds

injections.name: what-arrived-is-not-checked-against-what-left
injections.why: the transport's own defect, which is a different repair from a stale round: the bytes that arrived are not the bytes that were sent, and re-dispatching would answer about the copy again

injections.name: a-run-still-going-is-read-as-one-that-answered
injections.why: the sentinel is the ONLY thing that says a detached run is over — not the process, not the log going quiet, both of which this machine's remote-build rules were written after mis-reading. A model that assumes an ending reads a census still walking the tree as a census that found nothing

edits.to: let mut answer = Answer { sentinel: Some(0), ..Answer::default() };

injections.name: the-sentinel-is-only-looked-for-at-the-start-of-a-line
injections.why: the transport can leave the cursor where the wrapped command left it, so the launcher's append lands on the tail of another line. A reader anchored to line starts then answers `still running` about a run that ended — forever, which is a refusal that looks exactly like a gate working

injections.name: a-red-suite-elsewhere-is-read-as-a-clean-census
injections.why: the census is a reading of the run it rides on, so a suite that died early reached less — and a clean census over a shorter run is clean for a reason that has nothing to do with reaches. This is the arm that keeps `it passed there` from meaning `it did not get far enough to fail`

injections.name: the-fingerprint-forgets-the-working-tree
injections.why: the loosening direction of the tree's identity: with only the index read, every uncommitted edit is invisible and a census about the bytes before it reads as current. This is the direction that makes a STALE answer look fresh, which is the one that ships

injections.name: the-fingerprint-carries-the-commit
injections.why: the tightening direction of the same fact, and it is `bx`'s own spelling — correct for ITS question (is the far copy the same checkout) and wrong for this one. The dispatch happens at commit time and the reading after `HEAD` has moved, so a HEAD-relative identity calls those two different trees and this gate would refuse every round forever while looking exactly like a gate working

injections.name: a-placement-on-this-machine-is-dispatched-to
injections.why: the refusal that has to happen BEFORE any tree moves: a census placed here is the one thing this lane must never take for an answer, and `--explain-choice` exists so that decision costs nothing. A gate reading the presence of a host instead of the word `where=` passes a local placement that names an alias

injections.name: a-claim-is-recorded-beside-a-dispatch-that-failed
injections.why: the worst state this gate has. A claim written next to a launch that never happened sends the reader after an answer nobody is writing, and what it gets back is `not judged` about a machine that was never asked — a true sentence about the wrong thing

injections.name: the-same-bytes-are-dispatched-again-on-every-commit
injections.why: this runs from a hook, so it runs on every commit. A dispatch per invocation rsyncs the tree to a SHARED build machine over and over and leaves the previous census answering about bytes nobody is asking about — the cost lands on the fleet, where nothing in this repository would ever see it

injections.name: the-claim-does-not-name-the-bytes-it-sent
injections.why: without it there is nothing to hold the far side's header against, so a copy that arrived different and a tree that has since changed become one shape — and the dispatch loop above loses the only thing that tells it this question was already asked

injections.name: the-whole-log-is-tipped-into-the-hook
injections.why: measured on two real logs: 2,766 lines of which 17 decide, and 2,815 of which 23 do when the suite failed. Both callers are git hooks, so a gate that prints everything does not carry the finding to the person pushing — it buries it under the ordinary output of a passing suite, which is the one place a reader will not look

injections.name: a-suite-that-failed-elsewhere-is-shown-without-its-failure
injections.why: the other half of the same line. The census is a reading of the run it watched, so a red suite there is part of this gate's answer — and a reader handed the census's verdict without the assertion that failed has to go to another machine to find out what happened

injections.name: the-launcher-hands-the-run-the-transports-own-stdin
injections.why: measured on this machine's fleet, not imagined: the transport sends its remote half down stdin, and a wrapped command that inherits it reads the REST OF THE SCRIPT instead of EOF. The transport then dies on a fragment and the sentinel is never written — a run with no verdict at all, on the job nobody wants to repeat

injections.name: the-launcher-keeps-the-transports-descriptors
injections.why: MEASURED on this fleet before it was a hypothesis. With the redirection on the census instead of on the braces, `&` backgrounds the whole `&&` list and the subshell running it keeps the transport's stdout as its own fd 1 — so the connection stays open for the entire run and a dispatch that costs 23 seconds took 565. The census was right, the verdict was right, and the git hook did not come back: only the clock said anything
